body_coverage: Five unsectioned introductory paragraphs, all Theoretical Background, Methods, four Findings cases and cross-case analysis, Discussion, Limitations, Conclusions/Implications; both native tables. Nine-dimension model figure not visually checked; no figure-only claim.
design: Four women teachers selected from graduate-course reflections as moderately/highly agentic for STEM equity; elementary/middle grades,8–33years experience. Fall2023 retrospective60–90min interviews. Nine identity dimensions as a priori codes, thematic cross-case actions at classroom/school/community levels; no classroom observations or comparison with low-agency teachers.
parse_check: Native full argument and tables read. Melissa experience differs:Table1 eight years, case describes six classroom years, potentially distinct definitions unresolved. Coded dimension count is evidence in an interview, not a validated amount of identity. Lisa narrative mentions misalignment/behaviour priorities whereas cross-case discussion emphasises encouragement: retain both, not a simple binary supportive school classification.

moves.problem: A common equity commitment does not explain the different professional roles teachers take up.
moves.author_move: Pairs identity statements with actions and school conditions. Lisa delays larger roles despite encouragement; Riley builds peer support without top-down structure; Melissa pursues wider PD while taking school action slowly; Monique uses recognised authority across roles.
moves.project_inference: Use variation to refine how a condition works: support, recognition, readiness and available collaborations may shape the location and form of action differently. Develop a bounded explanation of action rather than rank commitment by how widely people act.
moves.condition: Reported actions from four positively selected cases; no causal identity-to-agency process or measured effects on student equity.

do_not_adopt: Eight/nine coded dimensions versus six/seven and wider actions is an observed case pattern, not a dose-response relation.
Lack of administrative support did not prevent all action; Lisa's encouragement did not entail immediate wider action.
Do not claim professional study or teachers' actions improved student equity outcomes, which were not measured.
Authors collected data within their programs; reported practice and social desirability remain material limitations.
correction_check: No comprehensive current correction/retraction verification; interpretive inconsistencies retained rather than repaired.
review_status: AI reading and project inference; human review pending
